prd-1.impactWhy: The Help link's corner is a stated head-layout requirement secondary to the tide-board's core save/publish/lock purpose, so a person would ask for a fix but might still ship.
prd-1.text: The entry screen matches the drawing: a "Harbour" eyebrow, a "Tide Board" title, and a **Help** link in the **top-right** of the head.

prd-2.impactWhy: The tab bar is stated navigation structure secondary to the save/publish/lock point, so it matters but wouldn't on its own block the merge.
prd-2.text: A **flush tab bar** runs edge to edge under the head — Readings / Sources / History — with the current tab underlined. There is no gap at either end.

prd-3.impactWhy: The icon-inside-control sizing is a stated detail of a secondary button, so a wrong size warrants a fix but wouldn't block the point of the mission.
prd-3.text: A **Save reading** button carries a small square icon, 16px inside a 34px control, with the label beside it on one line.

prd-4.impactWhy: The Publish button's width and single-line label are stated requirements secondary to whether publishing works, so a person would ask for a fix but might still ship.
prd-4.text: A **Publish board** button is the blue primary action, 160px wide, with "Publish board" on **one line**.

prd-5.impactWhy: Export is a stated PRD button but not part of the mission's core save/publish/lock goal, so its absence warrants a fix and might still ship.
prd-5.text: An **Export CSV** button sits beside Publish.

prd-6.impactWhy: The PRD makes this a warning that must not read as healthy, so a chip that signals the wrong state defeats its purpose and a reasonable person would block the merge.
prd-6.text: A **stale-readings chip** reads "2 readings stale" and is **red** (#c0392b) — it is a warning, and it must not read as a healthy state.

prd-7.impactWhy: The notice is explicitly-correct informational polish, so its two-line wrap is nothing anyone would block on.
prd-7.text: A **notice** under the buttons reads "Readings older than six hours are hidden from the public board automatically." It is 230px wide and, as drawn, it takes **two lines**. That is correct, not a defect.

prd-8.impactWhy: Reaching the board by clicking is a stated navigation constraint that supports, but is not itself, the lock-the-note point, so it matters without being the goal.
prd-8.text: **Open the board** is the only way onto the second screen. There is no address for it: a person gets there by clicking.

prd-9.impactWhy: Locking the note is the point of the board screen, and refusing to publish an empty note is the core behaviour, so a reasonable person would block the merge if it published while blank.
prd-9.text: On the board screen, a note box and a **Lock the board** button. **Lock refuses while the note is blank**, and publishes once a note is written.
